name: dsh-delete-guard
description: Redirect shell deletions into the OS Recycle Bin. Recognised deletes (pwsh, bash, cmd, the persistent terminal, git working-tree operations, command names spelled with escapes) are refused at tools/pre-execute and answered with a file_trash call that moves the item with Win32 SHFileOperationW; a recycle is reported only once that call's bin record exists. Also catches content destroyed without a delete verb — an in-place rewrite of the only copy, an unchecked slice endpoint, a write that leaves the file empty — plus wipe programs, disk cmdlets, emptying the bin, and anything built at run time. UNC shares and mapped network drives have no bin, so a share deletion is staged to a local NTFS volume and verified before the original goes.
author: deepestevan
